question_text: Your company is migrating a legacy ML pipeline from Azure ML SDK v1 to v2. The pipeline includes custom training scripts in Python and R, and you need to maintain the existing script structure while enabling reusable components. Which approach should you take?

options.A: Rewrite all scripts in PyTorch and use the Azure ML Python SDK v2 with auto-logging enabled
options.B: Wrap each script in a YAML component definition and reference them in a pipeline.yaml using CLI v2
options.C: Deploy each script as a separate Azure Function and trigger them via Azure Event Grid
options.D: Use the Azure ML designer to rebuild the pipeline visually without any code changes

question_text: A data engineer at Contoso needs to train a PyTorch model on a large dataset stored in Azure Data Lake Gen2. The training requires 4 NV6 VMs across 2 nodes for distributed training. Which compute and command configuration should they use?

options.A: Create a compute instance with Standard_NV6_v3 SKU and run az ml job create with --compute-target nv6-4node
options.B: Use a compute cluster with Standard_NV6_v3 and 2 nodes, then submit a job with distributed training enabled via YAML using MPI
options.C: Attach an Azure Kubernetes Service cluster and deploy the model via SDK v2 using ManagedOnlineEndpoint
options.D: Use serverless compute with Azure Spark and specify the PyTorch trainer in the pipeline YAML

question_text: You are setting up a secure Azure ML workspace for a financial services client. They require data to never leave the West Europe region and all secrets to be stored in Azure Key Vault. Which configuration ensures compliance?

options.A: Set region to West Europe during workspace creation and use Azure ML SDK v2 to reference Key Vault via service principal
options.B: Create the workspace in West Europe, enable VNet integration, and configure datastore connections using Key Vault secrets with az ml datastore create
options.C: Deploy a compute instance in East US, configure a private link to Key Vault, and use Azure CLI v1 for all asset creation
options.D: Enable Azure Purview for data lineage and store all model artifacts in Azure Blob Storage with SAS tokens

question_text: Your ML team needs to automate hyperparameter tuning for a scikit-learn model. The search space includes 3 numerical parameters and 2 categorical ones. You must visualize results and track experiments. Which toolchain should you use to minimize code changes and maximize integration with the studio?

options.A: Use Azure ML designer to drag-drop a hyperparameter tuning component and connect it to the training module
options.B: Write a script with optuna and submit via az ml job create referencing a YAML config with sweep parameters
options.C: Use Automated ML UI with custom metrics and enable hyperparameter tuning in the experiment settings
options.D: Deploy the model to a batch endpoint and call it from Azure Functions with random parameter selection

question_text: You are responsible for deploying a generative AI application powered by Llama 3 from Hugging Face. The app must support dynamic prompt chaining and be deployable to a real-time endpoint. Which Azure ML feature should you use?

options.A: Use the Model Catalog to import the Llama 3 model and deploy it via az ml endpoint create with a custom scoring script
options.B: Build the app using Prompt Flow, define the flow in a .flow file, and deploy it to a managed online endpoint using CLI v2
options.C: Use Microsoft Foundry’s Agent Service with the Hugging Face SDK and orchestrate via Azure Logic Apps
options.D: Deploy the model to Azure App Service with Flask and use Azure Functions for prompt orchestration

question_text: A team at Contoso wants to run an automated ML experiment for tabular data with 10M rows. They need to ensure the data is read efficiently and the experiment supports both regression and classification tasks. Which data type and environment should they select?

options.A: Use uri_file with a custom Docker image and specify the task type in the AutoML config YAML
options.B: Use mltable data abstraction and a curated environment like azureml-prebuilt-autml-gpu to enable AutoML optimizations
options.C: Store data as CSV in Azure Blob and use a compute instance with scikit-learn in a Conda environment
options.D: Use Azure Synapse Analytics with Spark and submit a pipeline via az ml pipeline create with distributed training

question_text: Your company needs to deploy a model that will be used for real-time scoring by 100K users globally. You must minimize latency, ensure high availability, and allow A/B testing between two model versions. Which deployment strategy should you implement?

options.A: Deploy to a batch endpoint with a large compute cluster and use Azure Traffic Manager for global routing
options.B: Deploy to a managed online endpoint with two deployments and configure traffic splitting via az ml endpoint update
options.C: Use Azure Functions with model loading in memory and Azure CDN for caching responses
options.D: Deploy to Azure Kubernetes Service with a custom ingress controller and use Helm for canary releases

question_text: You are setting up a Python development environment to interact with Azure ML using SDK v2. You already have a workspace and want to run notebooks locally without installing additional dependencies. Which configuration is both optimal and minimal?

options.A: Install the azure-ai-ml package in a virtual environment and use MLClient.from_config() with the downloaded config.json file
options.B: Use Azure ML compute instance and access JupyterLab via the studio UI without local setup
options.C: Install Azure CLI v2 and use az ml job create from command line without any Python setup
options.D: Use Visual Studio Code with the Azure ML extension and configure it to connect to the workspace via Azure CLI authentication

question_text: Your team is building an MLOps pipeline that triggers on a git commit and must run a model retraining job followed by deployment. The pipeline should be version-controlled and support rollback. Which integration should you use?

options.A: Use Azure DevOps with a YAML pipeline that calls az ml job create and az ml endpoint update with Git artifact references
options.B: Set up GitHub Actions to trigger an Azure Function that runs the training and deployment via SDK v2
options.C: Use Apache Airflow with the airflow-provider-azure-machinelearning to submit jobs and monitor runs
options.D: Configure Azure Event Grid to trigger a Logic App that invokes the Azure ML REST API for retraining and deployment

question_text: You need to run a Python script that trains a model using data from Azure Blob Storage. The script requires specific libraries and must be reproducible across team members. Which combination of environment and data reference should you use?

options.A: Create a custom environment with a conda YAML file and reference the data using a uri_folder path in the job YAML
options.B: Use a curated environment like azureml-prebuilt-sklearn-0.24-ubuntu18.04-py37-cpu and mount the Blob Storage as a datastore via MLClient
options.C: Deploy the script to an Azure Container Instance with a Docker image built from a requirements.txt file
options.D: Use serverless compute with Azure Functions that triggers on Blob storage events and references data via HTTP endpoints
